statement: For every infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space H, there is a point-ultraweakly closed proper convex cone K contained in the normal completely positive maps B(H) -> B(H) such that K_{Q,P} = CP_{Q,P} for every pair of finite-rank orthogonal projections P,Q. Explicitly, for a unit e, E = |e><e|, and A = 2E-I, the cone K = {Phi in CP^sigma : <e,Phi(A)e> <= 0} has these properties and is not cut--pad stable.
contribution: This is an exact counterexample to the full frozen assertion and supplies the complementary sharpness construction to the source's reconstruction theorem: point-ultraweak closedness alone does not permit reconstruction from all finite corner cones when cut--pad stability is removed. No priority, novelty, or open-status claim is made.
